title: unify-sdks-auth-retries-streaming-ergonomics-and-version-bump-1.14.0
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Bring Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to parity for auth and retry semantics, stabilize streaming ergonomics, and publish a coordinated version bump to 1.14.0. This PR consolidates behavior and small ergonomics improvements discovered while onboarding customers to Dedicated and Private runtimes.

What changed (high level): unified auth header handling and token refresh hooks across SDKs; standardized retry/backoff defaults and exposed configurable policies; improved streaming client ergonomics (auto-reconnect, resumed frames, simpler async iterator for Python/TS, context-based cancellation for Go); synced examples and changelogs; bumped SDK package versions to 1.14.0 and updated CI matrices.

Key goals: backward-compatible defaults, clearer upgrade path for customers using custom auth/retry logic, parity across languages so cross-platform examples behave the same, and a single coordinated release to reduce support churn.

Testing and rollout: ran full unit and integration suites across matrix (py37/py310, node16/node18, go1.20/go1.21), manual smoke tests against a staging inference cluster, and a canary rollout to internal customers before merge. Linear: ENG-2101 (sdk parity), ENG-2183 (streaming ergonomics).

Notes for reviewers: see individual SDK sections in the commits. No breaking changes to surface API expected for most users; a few edge cases when customers relied on previous default retry counts (noted in release notes).
